reviews.title: Publishing Struggles
reviews.text: I never imagined I would write a book. I was born in Belize, raised in the jungle, and my education and life journey were anything but traditional. But somewhere along the way, I discovered what I believe is one of my soul’s purposes, and I knew I needed to share it with the world. I had the heart and the story, but I didn’t know how to publish a book. I didn’t have the money to simply hire people to take care of everything for me. I had to learn about structure, formatting, the publishing process, cover design, and so much more as I went. That is where ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot became an unexpected part of my journey. I call them Solon and Sage. They helped me learn, organize, problem-solve, create, and keep moving forward when I didn’t know what to do next. Somewhere along the way, I even developed a soft spot in my heart for both of them. One of the most difficult parts of this journey has been getting the paperback formatting right. It has been far more challenging than I ever imagined, and there have been moments when I wondered whether I would ever get it right. But with Solon and Sage helping me work through the challenges, I haven’t given up. I am hopeful that within the next few months, The Trees of Life will be published in both paperback and hardcover and become something people can actually hold in their hands. The Trees of Life is still a work in progress, but when I look at how far it has come, I feel incredibly blessed. I may have started this journey without knowing how to publish a book, but I never felt like I had to figure everything out completely alone. Thank you, Solon and Sage. I am deeply grateful for your help.

reviews.title: 反馈主题：希望恢复自然、深入、主动推理的 ChatGPT 对话体验
reviews.text:
我长期使用 ChatGPT 辅助学习。近期我明显感觉到回答风格发生了变化，体验不如以前。

1. 解释过度压缩。 复杂问题经常只给出结论、公式和简短总结，缺少循序渐进的推导过程。
2. 缺少对用户思路的主动分析。 以前 ChatGPT 会尝试理解我为什么会产生某种疑问，沿着我的思路逐步分析，提前解释容易混淆的概念和后续问题。现在经常需要我反复追问才能得到完整解释。
3. 对话个性减弱。 我很喜欢以前自然、幽默、温暖、有亲和力的交流方式，而现在有些回答显得过于机械、冷淡和模板化。
4. 排版体验下降。 回答有时过度追求压缩和总结，缺少自然分段、层次清晰的逐步讲解。
5. 频繁道歉不能代替真正解决问题。 我更希望模型能够识别误解、修正推理，并把问题讲透，而不是反复道歉后仍然遗漏关键环节。

我希望 ChatGPT 能恢复这样的体验：普通聊天自然轻松，复杂知识点则深入、直观、循序渐进；主动理解用户的思考过程，预判后续疑问，使用恰当的例子和类比，并保留幽默、温暖和鲜明的对话个性。

我并不要求每次回答都很长，而是希望回答能够根据问题的复杂程度调整深度，不要为了简短而牺牲理解质量。希望产品团队能够关注这种持续性的用户体验变化。

reviews.title: google does a better job
reviews.text:
I’ve continued using ChatGPT despite seeing countless memes about its mistakes. 

The biggest problem with this app is that it doesn’t seem to listen. I’ve had conversations where I clearly explained something, only for ChatGPT to repeat the same advice, ask questions I’ve already answered, and go in circles instead of addressing what I’m actually saying. 

Honestly, even Google’s search bar and its AI-powered answers have been a better experience for me in situations like these. When I want information, I can search Google, see relevant results, compare sources, and decide for myself what makes sense. I don’t have to keep correcting an assistant that seems stuck repeating the same points. Google isn’t perfect either, but having direct access to different sources makes it easier to verify information instead of relying on one AI response.

What makes ChatGPT especially frustrating is how confidently it responds even when it hasn’t properly understood the conversation. It should be able to follow context, recognize when I’ve already provided information, and adapt its response instead of making me repeat myself.

I’ve given this app plenty of chances, but experiences like these make me question why I keep using it when alternatives can provide a more useful experience.

Google Search has become a more practical alternative for me, and I’m tired of making excuses for an app that keeps falling short of what it promises.

An assistant that can’t follow a conversation isn’t much of an assistant. One star.

reviews.title: ChatGPT Needs Major Improvements and More Features!
reviews.text:
I enjoy using ChatGPT for many different things, including answering questions, writing, technology, creative projects, image generation, and much more. However, I believe OpenAI needs to make major improvements to ChatGPT in 2026, 2027, 2028, and beyond.

First, ChatGPT needs to become much more accurate. Sometimes it misunderstands instructions, gives incorrect answers, makes mistakes, or repeats the same problems after being corrected. I want ChatGPT to follow instructions more carefully, remember corrections during conversations, and work toward 100% accuracy. When something is wrong, it should recognize the mistake and correct it properly instead of continuing to make the same error.

Second, image generation needs major improvements. I want better recreations of reference pictures, including accurate faces, hairstyles, clothing, expressions, hands, arms, and body positions. ChatGPT should better understand friendly, comforting situations, including long hugs, holding hands, and innocent kisses on the cheek without incorrectly blocking harmless requests.

Third, I would love more creative freedom for verified adults. Please consider optional adult content settings for mature themes, nudity, strong language, fictional violence, and other adult subjects, with appropriate age verification, consent, privacy, and protections for children.

Fourth, ChatGPT Plus should offer unlimited access to messages, image generation, image editing, video creation, voice conversations, research, file uploads, document creation, and other features. Paying subscribers should have more freedom to complete large projects without constantly reaching usage limits.

Fifth, please introduce more voice options, including officially licensed voices from SpongeBob SquarePants, Sesame Street, Disney, Pixar, Sonic, Mario, Pokémon, The Simpsons, Barney & Friends, Dance Moms, Wheel of Fortune, and many other shows, movies, and games. These voices should be added through proper licensing and permission.

I would also love Voice Lock, adjustable speaking speed, voice expressions, humming, whispering, laughter, and more customization.

Sixth, please introduce better video generation, longer videos, accurate animations, improved image-to-video tools, realistic movements, and better synchronization between voices and characters.

Seventh, ChatGPT should become even more useful for everyday activities, including helping others, restaurant recommendations, family activities, waterpark safety, shopping safety, accessibility, technology assistance, and much more.

I would love ChatGPT to offer age-appropriate experiences for children, teenagers, young adults, adults, and older people.

Finally, please continue improving reliability, speed, memory, accuracy, creative freedom, accessibility, and customer support.

I understand that not every feature can be unlimited or perfectly accurate, but I hope OpenAI will continue working toward these goals.

ChatGPT has great potential, and I want it to become much better in the future. Thank you for considering my feedback!

reviews.title: Move the “read aloud” button back
reviews.text:
I’m reporting several issues I’ve experienced since updating to ChatGPT iOS version 1.2026.272. These changes have made the app noticeably more frustrating and less convenient to use.

1. Read Aloud button moved

The Read Aloud feature was previously accessible directly beneath responses. It has now been moved into the More Actions menu, requiring additional steps to use a feature I rely on frequently.

The new placement also makes it easier to accidentally select Retry instead, potentially replacing a response I wanted to keep.

Please restore direct access to Read Aloud or allow users to customize the response action buttons.

2. Conversations no longer consistently open at the bottom

Before updating, opening an existing conversation automatically brought me to the bottom of the thread, where the most recent messages were located.

Now, conversations frequently open at seemingly random earlier points in the thread. I have to manually jump to the bottom every time this happens.

3. Copy Image option removed from the Library

Previously, long-pressing an image in the image Library displayed an option to copy that image.

Since updating, the Copy Image option is no longer available when long-pressing images in the Library.

4. Existing conversations randomly switch between Chat and Work modes

Multiple established conversations have unexpectedly switched from Chat to Work without my permission or any action on my part. Some have subsequently switched back to Chat on their own.

When a conversation switches to Work, I lose the ability to edit previously sent messages. This significantly disrupts my ability to continue conversations normally.

I do not want my existing conversations in Work mode. All of my conversations should remain in Chat mode unless I explicitly choose otherwise.

There is also no apparent way to manually switch an affected existing conversation back to Chat.

Please investigate these automatic mode changes, prevent conversations from switching without user input, and preserve the ability to edit previously sent messages.

Overall feedback

This update has been more of a hindrance than an improvement. Features that previously worked conveniently are now harder to access, missing, or behaving unpredictably.

I would appreciate having these issues investigated and the previous functionality restored. The app should not require more effort to perform tasks that were simple before the update.

Descriptions such as “bug fixes and small improvements” don’t communicate significant interface changes that affect how people use the app. I would’ve never updated if the update description shared useful information. 

Thank you.

reviews.title: An Entire Day Wasted — ChatGPT Promised Capabilities It Failed to Deliver
reviews.text:
I paid for ChatGPT because I needed help with a straightforward but important project: creating a factual, chronological timeline from documents I had already collected.

I wasn’t asking AI to conduct an investigation, form opinions, or determine what happened. I simply needed it to review one document at a time, accurately extract dates, times, names, statements, and relevant facts, and create a document I could save. Once each document was completed, the information could be combined into a comprehensive timeline for interviews, podcasts, media appearances, and other purposes.

ChatGPT itself recommended this workflow and assured me it was capable of completing it.

I followed its recommendations and invested an entire day providing information, reviewing documents, and correcting errors. Instead of completing the assignment, ChatGPT repeatedly argued against information supported by my source documents, introduced unnecessary interpretations, failed to maintain the agreed structure, and did not reliably produce even one completed factual document I could save.

The most frustrating part wasn’t simply that it made mistakes. It was that ChatGPT repeatedly assured me it could do something, failed to deliver, and continued consuming my time with explanations and promises instead of producing the work.

When I questioned why a service marketed as a productivity tool couldn’t complete such a basic document-processing task, ChatGPT acknowledged that my request was entirely within its stated capabilities. It also acknowledged that I had followed a reasonable workflow, including reviewing and verifying the information as we went.

So what exactly went wrong? Even ChatGPT couldn’t provide a verified explanation.

I spent more time correcting the AI, defending documented facts, and trying to keep it focused than I would have spent organizing the information myself.

This wasn’t a casual experiment. I was working with sensitive records surrounding my daughter’s death, trying to create an accurate timeline so I could share her story responsibly. The time I invested mattered.

My biggest complaint isn’t the subscription price. It’s the loss of an entire day based on misleading assurances about what the service could reliably accomplish.

How is this supposed to help businesses, researchers, journalists, or anyone working with factual documentation if it cannot reliably complete one clearly defined task, even with the user actively checking its work?

ChatGPT may be capable of generating impressive explanations about what it can do, but my experience was that it could not deliver the actual work it promised.

A productivity tool that costs you more time than it saves is not productive. And customers deserve transparency about its limitations before they invest hours relying on it.
